_note: Mock IT knowledge base for testing. Each article is a verified, approved fix.

articles.title: Account locked after failed login attempts
articles.symptoms: User sees 'Your account has been locked' after entering the wrong password several times.
steps: Confirm the account status is 'locked' using check_account_status.
Verify the employee's identity through the approved IT identity check.
IT staff unlocks the account from the admin console (agent must not do this itself).
Ask the employee to sign in and change the password if they are unsure of it.

articles.title: Password expired
articles.symptoms: Sign-in fails with 'Your password has expired' or VPN rejects the password.
steps: Confirm the account status is 'password_expired' using check_account_status.
Guide the employee to the self-service password portal to set a new password.
After changing it, reconnect to email and VPN with the new password.

articles.title: Account disabled
articles.symptoms: User sees 'This account has been disabled'.
steps: Confirm the account status is 'disabled' using check_account_status.
Do not re-enable the account. Disabled accounts need HR and security approval.
Escalate to a human IT administrator.

articles.title: VPN certificate expired or client outdated
articles.symptoms: VPN shows 'Certificate expired' or fails right after connecting.
steps: Confirm certificate_valid is false or client_up_to_date is false using check_vpn_status.
Install the latest approved VPN client from the company software portal.
Request a renewed VPN certificate through the IT portal; IT staff issues it.

articles.title: VPN authentication failed
articles.symptoms: VPN rejects the username or password.
steps: Check the account with check_account_status: VPN uses the same credentials.
If the account is locked or the password expired, fix that first (see KB-001 / KB-002).
Reconnect to the VPN after the account issue is resolved.

articles.title: VPN connection timed out
articles.symptoms: VPN keeps trying to connect then times out.
steps: Check the user's site network with check_network_status.
If the site network is up, ask the user to try another network (e.g. mobile hotspot).
Restart the VPN client and try again.

articles.title: Low disk space
articles.symptoms: Device is slow, updates fail, or 'Low disk space' warning appears.
steps: Confirm disk_free_percent is below 10 using check_device_status.
Empty the Recycle Bin and clear the Downloads folder of files no longer needed.
Run the built-in Disk Cleanup tool (Windows) or Storage Management (macOS).
Move large personal files to the approved company cloud storage.

articles.title: Device offline or missing updates
articles.symptoms: Device is not reporting to IT, or antivirus/patches are out of date.
steps: Confirm device_status and last_patch_date using check_device_status.
Connect the device to the company network or VPN so it can report in.
Run Windows Update / macOS Software Update and restart.
Update the antivirus definitions from the antivirus app.

articles.title: Suspected malware or security alert on device
articles.symptoms: Security alerts on the device, antivirus turned off unexpectedly, or strange network activity.
steps: Do not try to clean the device yourself and do not turn it off.
Disconnect the device from the network (unplug cable / turn off Wi-Fi).
Escalate immediately to the security team. This incident needs human review.

articles.title: Site network outage
articles.symptoms: Everyone at a site has no network access.
steps: Confirm network_status is 'down' using check_network_status.
If there is an active_outage_id, link the ticket to that outage instead of opening a new investigation.
Inform users that the network team is working on the outage.

articles.title: Slow or unstable site network
articles.symptoms: Network works but is slow or drops often.
steps: Confirm network_status is 'degraded' using check_network_status.
Note latency_ms and packet_loss_percent in the ticket for the network team.
Suggest a wired connection for critical work until the network team resolves it.
